title: Construction of the three induced derived-couple maps
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], and let $s\in\mathbf N$.
Let $D^{p,q},E^{p,q}$ be objects for $p,q\in\mathbf Z$, with maps
$a:D^{p,q}\to D^{p-1,q+1}$, $f:E^{p,q}\to D^{p+2,q-1}$,
and $g:D^{p,q}\to E^{p+s,q-s}$. Put $d^{p,q}=g^{p+2,q-1}f^{p,q}$.
Let $\beta^{p,q}:E^{p-s-2,q+s+1}\to E^{p,q}$ be the incoming $d$, with the
canonical transport of its target indices, and assume $d^{p,q}\beta^{p,q}=0$
and $f^{p+s,q-s}g^{p,q}=0$. Put
$D'^{p,q}=\operatorname{im}(a^{p+1,q-1})$ and
$E'^{p,q}=\operatorname{coker}(\widehat\beta^{p,q})$, where
$\widehat\beta$ is the lift of $\beta$ to $K^{p,q}=\ker d^{p,q}$.
Write $I^{p,q}:D'^{p,q}\to D^{p,q}$ for the transported image inclusion,
$A^{p,q}:D^{p+1,q-1}\to D'^{p,q}$ for the image epimorphism,
$P^{p,q}:K^{p,q}\to E'^{p,q}$ for the cokernel projection,
and $\widehat g^{r,t}:D^{r,t}\to K^{r+s,t-s}$ for the kernel lift of $g$.
All transports are the unique equality morphisms from the displayed integer identities.
Assume $\operatorname{im}f^{p,q}=\ker a^{p+2,q-1}$ and
$\operatorname{im}a^{p,q}=\ker g^{p-1,q+1}$ at every bidegree.
Then there exist maps $a':D'^{p,q}\to D'^{p-1,q+1}$,
$f':E'^{p,q}\to D'^{p+2,q-1}$, $g':D'^{p,q}\to E'^{p+s+1,q-s-1}$ satisfying the three defining equations
$I^{p-1,q+1}a'^{p,q}=a^{p,q}I^{p,q}$,
$I^{p+2,q-1}f'^{p,q}P^{p,q}=f^{p,q}\iota_K^{p,q}$,
and
$g'^{p,q}A^{p,q}=P^{p+s+1,q-s-1}\widehat g^{p+1,q-1}$,
with canonical target transport in the last equation.
These maps are unique. No exactness of the induced maps is asserted.

proof.text: Define a′ explicitly as the incoming image inclusion followed by the equality transport to the next a source and factorThruImage of that a. The image.fac equation and transport of the family a prove its restriction equation. The map-data structure stores only f′ and g′; its alpha method is this explicit map.

Obtain a followed by g equal to zero using kernelSubobject_factors_iff and imageSubobject_factors_comp_self after rewriting the image/kernel equality. Use the assumed image(a)=kernel(g) equality to get the image kernel universal property, via ShortComplex.exact_iff_image_eq_kernel and Exact.isLimitImage′. Lift the cycle restriction of f, transported to the exact codomain of a, into that image. Its composite with the lifted incoming boundary is zero, since after the mono image inclusion this composite is beta followed by f. The prescribed beta formula and transport of f reduce beta followed by f to f followed by g followed by f, zero by the g-then-f relation. Use cokernel.desc to obtain f′; cokernel.π_desc proves its equation.

Likewise obtain f followed by a equal to zero directly from the same Mathlib factorization lemmas. Lift each g into cycles, then compose with the cycle cokernel projection. Precomposing this map by the preceding f gives zero: after postcomposing by the mono kernel inclusion, f followed by the cycle lift of g agrees with the transported incoming beta lift; its cycle projection is zero by cokernel.condition. The assumed image(f)=kernel(a) equality gives Exact.isColimitImage, so descend through factorThruImage a to obtain g′. Transport to the successor bidegree and prove its equation. Choose these genuinely constructed families to assemble DerivedCoupleMapData. Mono image cancellation proves uniqueness for a′; epi cycle projection followed by mono image cancellation proves uniqueness for f′; epi image cancellation proves uniqueness for g′.

proof_origin.note: Complete Lean construction written by M1, following Stacks 011R setup (4)-(6) and 0AMJ. Alpha is the explicit image-factorization composite; forward descends a lift into the alpha image through the cycle cokernel; backward descends through ShortComplex.Exact.isColimitImage. All index transports are proved. Repair: zero composites are obtained directly from Mathlib kernelSubobject_factors_iff and imageSubobject_factors_comp_self; no duplicate zero-composite helper is declared.
